analysis: What changed vs the 8 AM brief: the rally firmed rather than faded into the late morning — S&P +5.1%, Nasdaq +6.8%, Dow +3.3% (~1,600 points) per Investopedia's late-morning update, with Seeking Alpha showing the S&P at 7,253.24 (+4.96%) around 10:40 AM ET. NVDA extended to +33-35% (~$168-170 vs Friday's $125.53 close), adding roughly $1 trillion in market value and retaking the No. 2 market-cap spot behind Apple; Reuters has the Nasdaq-100 on track for a $2T+ value surge, its biggest one-day gain since April 2025. New texture: Nasdaq-100 futures were briefly halted for volatility before the open, and Dell is now +24%, on pace for its largest daily percentage gain since May. The laggards sharpened the split: CrowdStrike's reaction deepened to -12% on the $43.9B all-stock Zscaler deal (ZS +14%), and Anthropic slipped to an $86.47 intraday low, still sitting out the rally. Gold extended to +4.5% ($3,675) and WTI deepened to -3.5% ($80.55, lowest since August), while the 10Y sits at 4.95-4.98% (+4-5 bps). What did NOT change: Capital Economics ('dead cat bounce') and BCA ('failed to find a floor') are still fading the move, the SEC accounting probe, Bessent's Nov 25 deadline and Huang's Dec 1 House testimony remain open, and the HN reinstatement thread (now 1,665+ points) still centers on the board's whiplash. Signal vs noise: the breadth of the chip/neocloud rebound, the $1T NVDA value add and the futures halt are signal — this is a positioning event, not a slow grind; the exact intraday percentages are noise in a thin Thanksgiving-week tape, and the close is the first real test of whether buyers hold after indices already eased off the open's peak.

community_signals.takeaway: The reinstatement thread is now at 1,665+ points and remains the day's dominant discussion — the community is dissecting the board's whiplash reversal, the US government input behind it, and whether the rally holds into the close, beyond what the headlines themselves say.

headlines.headline: Rally holding and firming into the late morning: S&P +5.1%, Nasdaq +6.8%, Dow +3.3% (~1,600 points) (Investopedia, ~11:30 AM ET), on pace for the best day since April 2025. Nasdaq-100 futures were briefly halted for volatility ahead of the open (Seeking Alpha). SPY +4.3% after the open (IBD); QQQ +6.8%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The bounce is not fading after the open — but the pre-open futures halt shows how disorderly the positioning was, and the close is the first real test in a thin holiday-week tape.

headlines.headline: Nvidia extended to +33-35% (~$168-170 vs Friday's $125.53 close), adding roughly $1 trillion in market value and retaking the No. 2 market-cap spot behind Apple (Investopedia, Reuters, USA Today). The Nasdaq-100 is on track for a $2T+ surge in value, its biggest one-day gain since April 2025. NVDA is still about 34% below its October record of $243 (Wall Street Sketched).
headlines.why_it_matters: The leadership vacuum is fully closed and the market is pricing Huang's return as worth ~$1T — but the stock is still a third below its October high, so this is a repair, not a new high.

headlines.headline: AI breadth stayed wide and deepened: Dell +24%, on pace for its largest daily percentage gain since May (Barron's); Micron +19-21%, TSMC +17%, Marvell +19%, Intel +12%, SMH +15-17%, SOXX +13%, memory ETF DRAM +19%; CoreWeave and Nebius +27-28% each, Lumentum +19%+ (Investopedia, Barron's, IBD).
headlines.why_it_matters: The rebound is not just Nvidia — semis, memory, neocloud and server names are all lifting together, which is what a durable bounce needs; Dell's record-style day shows partners are being re-rated too.

headlines.headline: Megacaps all green: Tesla +13%, Alphabet +6%, Meta +6%, Amazon +3%, Microsoft +3%, Apple also higher (Investopedia). Caterpillar +7% in the Dow (IBD).
headlines.why_it_matters: Every Mag 7 name is up together for the first time in days — the rally is broad-based across big tech, not a single-stock spike.

headlines.headline: CrowdStrike (CRWD) fell 12% after announcing its all-stock deal to acquire Zscaler (ZS), valued at about $43.9B; Zscaler jumped 14% (Investopedia; IBD had CRWD -8% premarket, ZS +19%).
headlines.why_it_matters: The market is voting against the deal's price even on a huge up day — a $44B all-stock acquisition dilutes holders, and the -12% reaction is the day's clearest single-name divergence.

headlines.headline: Anthropic (ANT) is down ~1% around $88, sitting out the rally — it swung between $84.79 and $94.24 and touched an $86.47 intraday low (Investopedia, Sovereign Magazine). Friday's close was $88.91; the $83 IPO price is still the line in the sand below.
headlines.why_it_matters: The newest mega-IPO is not joining the relief rally after Friday's 8.5% drop — buyers are still selective, and IPO euphoria has not returned.

headlines.headline: Rates and havens: 10-year Treasury yield 4.95-4.98%, up 4-5 bps from Friday's 4.94% (IBD, Investopedia). Gold futures +4.5% to $3,675 after Friday's 15-month low; WTI crude -3.5% to $80.55, lowest since August; bitcoin ~$62,600-63,100, up ~3-4% (Investopedia, IBD).
headlines.why_it_matters: Yields ticking up while gold also rallies is the tension in the tape — bonds are not pricing a Fed pivot, and gold's bounce is a recovery from Friday's washout, not a new haven bid.
